summary: The Playwright tests are syntactically correct, use Playwright APIs properly, and include the required testCaseIds in titles. However, some assumptions in selectors and assertions weaken the tests, and some assertion patterns are suboptimal. The tests would benefit from stronger, more explicit selectors and assertions to ensure robust verification of correct categories and product filtering.

issues.description: Selectors such as getByRole('link', { name: 'Electronics' }) are based on assumptions about the category link being identifiable by role 'link' with a visible name, which may not be stable if UI changes. The product items are selected by a generic '.product-item' class, which may not discriminate products well.
issues.recommendation: Use more specific and stable selectors or test IDs where possible to improve resilience of tests against UI changes.

issues.description: The test for filtered products uses expect(products).not.toContain('SomeOtherCategoryProduct') relying on a hardcoded invalid product name without context, which may be fragile and unclear.
issues.recommendation: Use explicit product lists or better properties to verify the filtered products, or check product counts/types explicitly.

issues.description: The assertion await expect(page.title()).resolves.toMatch(/Electronics/) uses a promise matcher on page.title(), which is acceptable but less idiomatic than await expect(page).toHaveTitle(/Electronics/).
issues.recommendation: Use Playwright's built-in page expectation APIs like toHaveTitle for clearer and more consistent assertions.

recommendations: Strengthen selectors by using test IDs or data attributes instead of inferred roles or class names.
Replace promise-based assertion on page.title() with more idiomatic Playwright page expectation.
Improve product filtering test by verifying presence of only expected products rather than relying on absence of a single product name.
